sections.h2: What are the quickest ways to sell a Parma house?
sections.html:
A Parma owner can hire a broker, market the property without one, or sell to a cash buyer who accepts the place with its flaws. Parma is a large, densely built suburb where many houses date from the postwar decades, so buyers often negotiate over age-related items. A cash sale removes repair requests and mortgage appraisals from the schedule.

  • Hire a broker if the roof, windows and mechanical systems are sound and you can wait through a buyer's loan process.
  • Sell on your own when a closing agent or lawyer will prepare the contract and deed.
  • Pick cash for an estate house, a vacant property, a loan in arrears, or repair bills you would rather avoid.

Parma also keeps city registrations for rentals, vacant homes and foreclosure filings, covered below, and any of them can affect how fast a sale moves.

sections.h2: How did Parma grow into Ohio's largest suburb?
sections.html:
Parma is the largest suburb in Ohio and the second-largest city in Cuyahoga County, about 8 miles south of downtown Cleveland. The 2020 census counted 81,146 residents, and the estimate for mid-2025 is 78,581, the seventh highest in the state. The land was surveyed in 1806 as Township 6, Range 13 of the Western Reserve, settlers called it Greenbriar, and in 1826 the township took the name Parma after the Italian city.

Farming dominated until the 1920s. Parma incorporated as a village on December 15, 1924, then became a city on January 1, 1931, with 13,899 residents. A garden-city project called Ridgewood Gardens began in 1919, and the postwar boom lifted the count from 28,897 in 1950 to 82,845 in 1960 and a peak of 100,216 in 1970. It has eased down since.

The city spans 20.07 square miles. Cleveland and Brooklyn lie to the north, Brooklyn Heights and Seven Hills to the east, North Royalton and Broadview Heights to the south, and Brook Park, Middleburg Heights and Parma Heights to the west. The Henninger House of 1849, the oldest home still standing in Parma, occupies one of the higher points in the county.

sections.h2: What do income and value figures reveal about Parma?
sections.html:
Parma packs about 4,000 people into each square mile, and its median owner-occupied home is valued at $170,100, with nearly three in four homes lived in by their owners.

sections.h2: How do Parma's roads and schools figure in a sale?
sections.html:
The north-south spine includes West 130th Street, Ridge Road (State Route 3), State Road (State Route 94) and Broadview Road (State Route 176), which links to downtown Cleveland by way of the Jennings Freeway. East-west traffic uses Brookpark Road (State Route 17), Snow Road, West Ridgewood Drive, West Pleasant Valley Road and Sprague Road, with Interstate 480 just beyond the northern line and Pearl Road (U.S. Route 42) crossing a short stretch of the north. Most major streets carry a 35 mph limit, and Greater Cleveland RTA buses serve the city.

The Parma City School District serves Parma, Parma Heights and Seven Hills with six elementary schools, three middle schools and two high schools, Normandy and Valley Forge. The former Parma Senior High School ran from 1953 to 2023. Padua Franciscan High School is the private option, eight private primary schools operate in the city, and both Cuyahoga Community College and Bryant and Stratton College have campuses here.

sections.h2: Which Parma permits and registrations could slow a sale?
sections.html:
The Building Department requires a permit before work starts, and begins charging an administrative penalty when work starts without one: $100 for a first offense, $300 for a second and $500 for a third. Contractors must register with the department too, at $250 if work begins before registration is final. Windows, siding and roofing jobs each have their own permit application, and so do fences, sheds, garages, driveways and pools.

If you replaced a roof or added a deck without a permit, settle it before you list. The city's fence application also asks for either a state-registered surveyor's boundary survey or consent from neighbors.

Parma attaches these registrations to particular property situations:

  • Residential rental registration: $150 per property, certificates lapse each December 31, and a $50 late fee applies.
  • Notification of foreclosure filing: $100 for a one-, two- or three-family residence.
  • Vacant residential property registration: $200, valid for one year.
  • Multiple dwelling registration: $100 for mixed-use buildings and apartment buildings with one to four suites.

The city says each of these can be completed online. Ask the Building Department whether any registration is tied to your address before you accept an offer.

sections.h2: What do Cuyahoga County rules mean for taxes and recording on a Parma sale?
sections.html:
Parma sits in Cuyahoga County, where the Fiscal Officer values property and the Treasurer collects. Tax runs a year behind, so calendar 2023 bills, for example, belong to tax year 2022. The county's 2026 calendar set first-half payments for February 19 and second-half payments for August 13, with a 10 percent penalty on late payments.

A late payer can request penalty relief on DTE Form 23A. The Treasury reviews it first, then the Fiscal Office, and the Board of Revision decides cases where a reasonable-cause box is checked. Its decision is final unless you appeal to the Board of Tax Appeals within 30 days.

An owner who thinks the value is too high can file a valuation complaint from the start of January to March 31, and e-filing is the board's preferred method. The complaint must state an exact opinion of value, and the board warns it may raise a value if the evidence supports it. If the Fiscal Office denies a homestead or owner-occupancy application, the denial can be appealed within 60 days of the letter. Where the county has filed an expedited tax foreclosure, the property may go to sheriff sale or to a land bank.

The county Fiscal Officer's Transfer and Recording division records deeds and asks for a DTE 100 form with each transfer. Since October 24, 2024 recording has cost $39 for the first two pages and $8 for each page after. Section 5302.30 of the Ohio code also has you give buyers a property disclosure form, unless the transfer is exempt.

faqs.q: Must I register a Parma rental house before selling it?
faqs.a: Yes, while it is a rental. Parma charges $150 for each rental property, certificates end every December 31, and a $50 late fee applies if the due date passes.

faqs.q: Does Parma make owners register vacant houses?
faqs.a: The city runs a vacant residential property registration at $200 with a one-year certificate. Ask the Building Department whether your house falls under it before listing.

faqs.q: What if a Parma house is in foreclosure?
faqs.a: The city asks for a notification of foreclosure filing at $100 for one-, two- and three-family homes. Contact the Building Department about the filing, and ask a closing agent how a sale would pay off the loan.

faqs.q: Can I contest my Parma valuation before a sale?
faqs.a: Yes. The county Board of Revision accepts complaints from the first of January to March 31, requires an exact opinion of value, and expects evidence such as a recent sale, an appraisal or repair estimates.

faqs.q: Will a cash buyer take a Parma house with unpermitted work?
faqs.a: Often, because the buyer takes the property as it stands. Report what you know on the Ohio disclosure form, and ask the Building Department what the city would need to close out an old permit.
